newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia rebels in new strike at gateway to Bogota.
newsitem.headline: Colombia rebels in new strike at gateway to Bogota.

text.p: Leftist rebels launched an assault on an army base at the southern gateway to Bogota just after nightfall on Thursday, killing at least one soldier and wounding several others, the government said.
An unknown number of Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) guerrillas attacked the base in a rural area close to the town of Usme, about 15 miles (25 km) south of the capital.

The firefight came just 48 hours after four days of fighting ended in the mountain community of San Juanito, 30 miles (50 km) east of the capital. The army said 16 soldiers died in that battle and scores of others were wounded.

"The rebels launched the attack on an army training base near Usme and killed at least one soldier who was shooting from a trench. But they fled when reinforcements arrived," Defence Minister Guillermo Gonzalez told the Radionet news network.

Gen. Euclides Sanchez, commander of the 13th army brigade based in Bogota, said the raid was a diversionary tactic to relieve pressure on the FARC column he said was being pursued in the mountains around San Juanito.

"This is a tactic to distract us and reduce pressure in other areas. But this is of little consequence because the rebels fled when reinforcements arrived. They don't stand and fight, but just strike and run off," Sanchez said.
Hundreds of troops have been airlifted into the area around San Juanito since the weekend to hunt down the guerrilla forces.
